name: Workshop - Streamline Telco (Churn Save on the Call)
narrative:
Rae Nakamura, a non-technical SVP of Customer Care & Retention, opens the care-agent console and sees what the contact center has been fighting for three weeks: a cluster of subscribers glowing red — churn risk spiking after a network outage on their service node collided with a billing issue and a competitor's promo. The save moment is on the call, but agents working from last-night's screen can't see the history in time.

Rae pulls up the worst account: subscriber SUB-0000214, a five-year customer with a churn-risk score of 0.86, an unresolved outage ticket on their node, and a billing dispute — why are they at risk, and what should the agent offer? The assistant surfaces the reason (the outage + the bill, not price alone) and ranks the three plays (a plan-upgrade discount, a one-time bill credit, or a device upgrade), each with the expected churn reduction and the customer's lifetime value at stake, from a heuristic scored on Streamline's own retention history. It recommends the bill credit, drafts the call-resolution summary, and stops for approval. Rae approves; the retention offer writes back to Lakebase with an audit trail — governed subscriber data turned into an on-call action, fast at full contact-center concurrency, with the assistant's AI spend capped and predictable per call.

Workshop training template (Tech Summit FY27 Live Days): data generator + full spec set (SDP pipeline, metric views, churn model, dashboard + Genie, and a Databricks App with a Visualize/Assist/Act agent loop over Lakebase). Maps to the three build milestones — Lakebase, Databricks Apps, Unity AI Gateway.
